questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
Find the integrating factor $\text{IF}$ and general solution of the linear differential equation in [Differential Equations]:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2x}{1 + x^2} y = \frac{1}{(1 + x^2)^2}$$
questions.solution: Here $P(x) = \frac{2x}{1 + x^2}$. The integrating factor is $\text{IF} = e^{\int \frac{2x}{1+x^2}dx} = e^{\ln(1 + x^2)} = 1 + x^2$. Multiplying gives $\frac{d}{dx}[y(1 + x^2)] = \frac{1}{1 + x^2} \implies y(1 + x^2) = \int \frac{dx}{1 + x^2} = \arctan x + C$.
questions.explanation: Solve using rigorous mathematical proofs and transformations in Differential Equations.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
Evaluate the integer value of the limit in [Differential Equations]:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} \times 6$$
questions.solution: Using Taylor series $\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + O(x^5)$, we have $\frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} = \frac{1}{6} + O(x^2) \to \frac{1}{6}$. Multiplied by $6$, the value is $1$.
questions.explanation: Derive using rigorous mathematical theorems in Differential Equations.
